payload.title: memory.append_jsonl still accepts memory/learning-events.jsonl with any event_type, and the one-owner scan and its pins exempt or compare only the whole memory.py module, so the closed learning-event vocabulary and the single-writer claim are not enforced at the door or inside the owner module
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/memory.py:29-36 (the journal filename sits in the surface map that memory.append_jsonl reads)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/memory.py:39-43 (append_jsonl stores any row for that file name; no event-type check)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/memory.py:1870-1871 (the closed-vocabulary refusal lives only in record_learning_event)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/ownership_atlas.py:150-153 (one_owner_offenders skips the owner's whole module although the family owner is the symbol memory.py:record_learning_event)
aria-kernel/tests/invariants/test_atlas_one_owner.py:101-109 (the writers pin compares module paths only, so a second writer function inside memory.py stays green)
aria-kernel/tests/test_learning_ledger_one_writer.py:96-115 (the vocabulary tests call only the owner; none asserts that memory.append_jsonl refuses the journal path)
payload.rule_violated: Single owner with no second door (CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 1, make it impossible; PLAN-v2 learning journal: record_learning_event is the only writer with a closed kind vocabulary)
payload.notes: At d716541239 a probe shows record_learning_event raising learning_event_unknown_kind for the kind anything_goes while memory.append_jsonl(root / 'memory' / 'learning-events.jsonl', {'event_type': 'anything_goes'}) returns the row and load_jsonl reads it back. Outside memory.py the literal shapes are red in the one-owner scan, and the alias and variable-path shapes are tracked as ARIA-MEDIUM-924, so this candidate is the open runtime door plus the module-wide exemption. A second function inside memory.py that appends the journal is not reported by one_owner_offenders (probed: offenders stay empty); the byte-pinned atlas only forces a regeneration, and every writer pin compares module paths, so two writers inside memory.py end green after the regeneration. Close condition: Make memory.append_jsonl refuse the learning-events path (route record_learning_event through append_declared_jsonl and keep load_jsonl for reads, the way F1.1 removed the journal from pr_tracking's surface map) and compare the owner symbol, not the module, in the atlas pins and in one_owner_offenders. Prove it with a test that memory.append_jsonl on the journal path raises GovernanceError and that a planted second writer function inside memory.py is reported. Plan row: F1.1 (the reader half of ARIA-LOW-732 stays with F1.2). Verified at origin/main d716541239.
